fit.gap_handling_summary: Gaps (GCP, graph modelling, Portuguese, Kubernetes) are not faked; the letter explicitly states cloud experience is in AWS and frames the overlap honestly. Query optimisation and governance are shown through closest real work.

issues: Snowflake cost figures lack a currency
Summary in third person ('Owns') while bullets are first-person implied ('Own', 'Mentor')

missed_but_candidate_has: query optimisation (only implied through build-time and incremental model work)
ats.reason: Clean, ordered extraction with standard headings and most supported must-haves in searchable form; query optimisation is only implied, and GCP is correctly not claimed.

issues: Does not use company values or culture (Together, Ownership, Pace)
Awkward phrasing 'Your support for open-source contributions is particularly relevant to my two merged...'
Largely restates CV bullets; no mention of the streaming/CDC work or hybrid openness
strengths: Links reusable-framework focus of the ad to her work
Honest about AWS vs Google Cloud
No stale framing from the old Kovalent Pay letter

spacing_issues: Noticeable empty area at bottom of CV page 1 before Kovalent Pay entry moves to page 2

fluency_and_tone_issues: 'Your support for open-source contributions is particularly relevant to my two merged Airflow provider pull requests'

requests.request: Please write my CV first, then the cover letter.
requests.evidence: Both CV and cover letter produced

evaluation.summary: A strong, honest package: every claim traces to the CV, portfolio or notes, and valuable notes facts (AWS certification, cost savings, on-call, talk, CDC) were added. Gaps such as Google Cloud are handled candidly in the letter rather than faked. The ATS text is clean and well-sectioned. Weaknesses are minor: dropped location, currency-less cost figures, some whitespace on CV page 1, and a letter that mostly restates the CV without using company values.
